As I mentioned in a previous post, I recently became a gymnastics coach for children. There are a couple of deaf students in one of the classes, so I enrolled in a sign language course at my university.

The thing about deaf people is that they have a very unique culture and behavior. The separate language has created a really interesting and unique community where customs are different from the ones we know. For instance, it is normal for them to not show up somewhere on time, and they take an extremely long time to say goodbye at group gatherings. One of the characteristics of this community is that they are very blunt. Their language is such that they don't really have a way to "mince words", if you will, so they just say what's on their mind.

So these two boys (adopted brothers) have an interpretor that goes with them into the class. He's tolerable, but he has an enormous beer belly. He is often seen lagging far behind the rest of the group when we move from one place to another, and always tries to find a mat or something to sit on. One time, I notice one of the deaf boys signing to him from across the floor. The interpreter laughs, and the boy signs something else. I look back and ask what he was saying.

"Oh, he's making fun of my belly. Those two always joke about how my belly jiggles when I laugh."

I just thought that was hilarious. Deaf people are awesome shitlords.

The 'Athens Affair' shows why we need encryption without backdoors

For refence, http://www.cyberciti.biz/hardware/howto-linux-hard-disk-encryption-with-luks-cryptsetup-command/ is a good guide to set up LUKS (which is encryption part of the linux kernel, so you have security and confidence that its by well known and skilled devs, and reviewed by thousands fo eyes, then some more obscure unknown software will many, many fewer devs)

This is good for whole partions/external devices, so USB drives and the likes (or your OS if you set it up at time of install)

So if you have some important files/porn, you should use this on your external drive, as your computer won't have any of the speed hits from booting from an encrypted drive, but you'll have the security of encryption of your important files, as well as being able to physically take the drive with you if needed.

For single files in your OS, there is file system level encrpytion in ext4, but its not that strong, so you should use:

http://www.cyberciti.biz/tips/linux-how-to-encrypt-and-decrypt-files-with-a-password.html gpg.

Remember if you have multiple files, you can always encrypte them after you put them into a tarball or some similar compression, or put them into a virtual file system.

Don't forget to securly delete the unencrypted file once the encrypted file is created. Using something like shred

https://askubuntu.com/questions/57572/how-to-delete-files-in-secure-manner

or do this all in a ram disk

http://www.cyberciti.biz/faq/howto-create-linux-ram-disk-filesystem/

While there are many other tools for encryption (like Veracrpyt, truecrypt, cipher shed) I am more trusting of tools under a much higher standard and viewed by more eyes, since both GNUpgp and LUKS are core parts of the GNU/Linux ecosystem, vs veracrypt.

While all these guides are from command line, there exists GUI toos too, how ever I recommend against them as it abstracts from what its actually happening, and creates another, rather large, attack surface.

For windows(10 specifically) and MacOSX? You've already lost more than half the battle, so theres not much use. Sure there is pgp and LUKS tools on MacOSX and windows (https://github.com/t-d-k/LibreCrypt for LUKS on windows), but you're already doing it on a very insecure platform.

(that how ever is not to say Linux/FLOSS OSes have won the battle, there is always bugs/security issues, but you can harden you FLOSS OS, the remaining battles for security on Linux is a FLOSS bootloader, like coreboot/libreboot to replace *EFI/BIOS, and FLOSS firmware for devices, and FLOSS drivers, as well as no binary blobs. How ever some of this extreamly hard if not impossible on current hardware, so you'll either need a Free Software Fondation approved computer, like what Richard Stallman has, or hopefully Libre/OpenSource hardware is able to previal, like openRISC. Which will be easy enough for linux users to switch over as we can just compile our stuff for it, but impossible for macOSX/Windows users to switch as they can't. The remaining software will probably end up being games,which sadly will probably need powerful hardware in order to emulate intel86_64 to run, or perhaps use FLOSS games. My favorite being Terasology, which is a voxel game with modAPI, cubic chunks, etc)
